source_text: (24) Στίχ. ζ΄. Καὶ ἀναλαβὼν τὴν παραβολήν. Ἡθεία Γραφὴ ἔν τισιν τόποις προκρίνει καὶ προτίθηοι τὸ συμβολικὸν ὂν τῆς ἱστορικῆς διηγήσεως ἐν τῇ αὐτοῦ ὑποθέσει.
thought_title: Scripture prefers symbolic meaning over historical narrative
orientation: Origen is commenting on Numbers 24:7, where Balaam takes up his oracle, and he pauses to state a principle about how Scripture sometimes works.
pass_a_gloss: Verse 7. And having taken up the oracle. The divine Scripture in some places prefers and sets before the symbolic meaning of the historical narrative in its own subject matter.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'oracle' for Balaam's prophetic utterance, not 'parable'.
The glossary requires 'symbolic meaning' for this term.
Both verbs are kept distinct to preserve the double action: Scripture both chooses the symbolic meaning and places it in front of the historical narrative.
The phrase is rendered literally to preserve the reflexive force of 'αὐτοῦ' referring to the symbolic meaning's own subject matter.

pass_b_english: Verse 7. And having taken up his oracle. In certain places the divine Scripture prefers the symbolic meaning and sets it before the historical narrative in its own subject matter.
